Q1: Boron shows known hazards for oral and organ/systemic toxicity (Tier 1) and expanded hazards for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity, environmental concerns, inhalation, and dermal/eye effects (Tier 2). Endocrine disruption remains a data-deficient area (Tier 4).
Q2: Boron is identified as a contaminant of concern under the Safe Drinking Water Act and is included in the EPA's Drinking Water Standard. It is not listed on any low hazard lists, suggesting it is not generally considered of low concern by regulatory bodies.
Q3: Boron is exceptionally well-characterized, evidenced by over 211,000 literature references and its well-defined elemental structure. It has undergone rigorous evaluation by the EPA's IRIS program and has a substantial number of toxicity records, indicating a comprehensive understanding of its hazards, with only one data-deficient hazard class (endocrine disruption).
